children: Altcoin spot trading volume, measured against Bitcoin, has now dropped below where it sat over the summer. That reverses a speculative surge that peaked only weeks ago.
In September 2026, altcoin spot volume relative to Bitcoin peaked near 4x. By late October, that ratio had slid to around 3x, and it stayed in that range heading into November.
Bitcoin dominance was approximately 60.5-61% from late October through mid-November. A dominance reading in that range means Bitcoin accounts for well over half the market by value.

The Altcoin Season Index, a gauge that tracks how altcoins perform against Bitcoin, requires a reading of 75 to declare an "altseason." In mid-to-late November, the index printed values between 45 and 48, pointing to what traders call Bitcoin Season conditions.
Total altcoin market capitalization fell by about $800 billion over roughly a month, settling around $1.06 trillion.

Ethereum, the largest altcoin, has not been spared. Its troubles have been compounded by steady redemptions from US spot Ether ETFs. Those funds recorded consecutive weeks of net outflows, totaling roughly $802 million in the first half of November.
ETF flows act as a window into institutional appetite. When money leaves week after week, it signals that larger investors are trimming exposure rather than buying the dip.
Analysts at Glassnode and Bitfinex have pointed to signs of potential selling exhaustion near Bitcoin's summer lows. The catch is that nobody has confirmed a bottom yet.

In previous market cycles, sharp spikes in altcoin activity often served as early warnings that Bitcoin was near a top. Sentiment then contracted, and capital flowed back into the leading asset. The September peak near 4x fits that template. Traders piled into riskier tokens, activity spiked, and then the enthusiasm drained away as conditions cooled.
A falling altcoin-to-Bitcoin volume ratio suggests investors are seeking relative safety in Bitcoin as the altcoin market cools. Bitcoin's dominance near 61% reinforces that view.

For altcoin holders, a combination of weaker volume, an index reading in the 40s, and roughly $802 million in Ether ETF outflows points to a market where speculative demand has thinned out considerably. Thinner trading in smaller tokens can mean wider spreads and sharper price swings when large orders hit the book.

Traders will want to see whether the altcoin volume ratio stabilizes around 3x or keeps sliding. A climb in the Altcoin Season Index back toward 75 would suggest risk appetite returning. Ether ETF flows are another key tell: a reversal from outflows to inflows would hint that institutions are warming back up to the largest altcoin.

title: Bitcoin consolidates capital as altcoin froth dissipates
